raw_case_text:
A 68-year-old Caucasian female was admitted to our Clinic on August 24, 2020, for exacerbating dyspnea and chest and right upper abdominal pain, accompanied by confusion for 3 weeks.
Five months earlier, in March 2020, she underwent radical right nephrectomy due to a CCRCC (tumor stage: pT3a, pNx, R0, M0). During the primary diagnosis, the blood analysis showed a white blood cell (WBC) count of 7,450/mul (reference range: 4,000-7,000/mul) with 1.1% (reference range: 1-6%) of eosinophilic granulocytes.
A computed tomography (CT) scan performed in July 2020, 3 months after the nephrectomy, revealed a retroperitoneal tumor mass in the surgical bed with hepatic and diaphragmatic invasion, and right pleural metastases. Histopathological assessment of liver infiltrates confirmed the diagnosis of local CCRCC relapse. During the diagnosis of tumor recurrence, the blood analysis showed a WBC count of 17,560/mul with 12.8% of eosinophilic granulocytes (AEC: 2,250/mul).
When abdominal pain and dyspnea occurred, palliative treatment with dexamethasone, pantoprazole, and buprenorphine were initiated. Moreover, targeted therapy for CCRCC was planned for the patient, but due to the rapid deterioration of health condition and a further increase of eosinophilic granulocyte count, the patient was admitted to our Clinic of Internal Medicine.
The past medical history also revealed that the patient had hypertension well controlled on bisoprolol only and underwent skin-sparing right mastectomy in 2005 for breast cancer (mammography and ultrasonography examination of the breasts, performed in August 2020, excluded the tumor recurrence). The patient had no history of alcohol abuse, asthma, or other allergic diseases.
On the day of admission to our Clinic, on examination, the patient appeared alert with mild functional cognitive disorder. Tachypnea and dullness over the right lung, up to seven intercostal spaces, were observed with the absence of breath sound. Abdomen tenderness during palpations and mild edema in distal parts of the lower limbs were also noticeable. Preliminary blood tests showed an increased C-reactive protein level of 240 mg/l, a WBC count of 40,770/mul, marked eosinophilia with an eosinophil count of 6,530/mul, mild anemia with a hemoglobin level of 11.6 g/dl, and a normal platelet count of 346,000/mul. A CT angiography of the chest revealed right-sided pleural effusion, pneumonia, and pulmonary microembolism.
Thoracentesis was performed for pleural effusion, and treatment with a broad-spectrum antibiotic (intravenous) and low-molecular-weight heparin (subcutaneous) were initiated. At that time, dexamethasone was discontinued due to the suspicion of infection disease and in purpose to carry out the differential diagnosis of hypereosinophilia. Despite the treatment, a further increase in leukocytes up to 56,000/mul with 33% of eosinophilic granulocytes (AEC: 18,500/mul) was observed.
Paraneoplastic eosinophilia is mainly associated with hematologic malignancies, although there is fairly extensive literature about eosinophilia in solid tumors, which mainly include case reports ( Table 2 ).
Several tests were performed to rule out the noncancer causes of hypereosinophilia. There was no clinical or serologic evidence of an allergy, a parasitic infection, or vasculitis. Blood tests showed a normal total immunoglobulin E (IgE) level of 59.2 kUa/l (normal < 81 kUa/l), while specific IgE for Aspergillus fumigatus or antibodies against myeloperoxidase were not detectable. A bone marrow biopsy was performed which showed no evidence of leukemia. Fluorescent in situ hybridization showed no FIP1L1-PDGFRa fusion. The temporal appearance of eosinophilia and recurrence of CCRCC without any other apparent potential causes confirmed the paraneoplastic nature of hypereosinophilia in our patient.
A massive intravenous dose of corticosteroids (1.5 g methylprednisolone) was initiated, which caused a profound, albeit transient, decrement in the eosinophil count ( Figure 1 ). Unfortunately, the patient's condition further deteriorated despite the treatment, and so targeted therapy for CCRCC was not initiated. We discontinued the corticosteroids after three days to limit their toxicity. Due to the poor prognosis, the patient received only palliative support and succumbed to the disease 6 months following surgery and 2 months after the diagnosis of tumor recurrence. Permission for a postmortem examination of the body was not granted.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 68-year-old Caucasian female presented 5 months after right radical nephrectomy for clear cell renal cell carcinoma with a 3-week history of worsening dyspnea, right chest and upper abdominal pain, and mild confusion.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Five months after undergoing radical right nephrectomy in March 2020 for stage pT3a clear cell renal cell carcinoma (CCRCC, with a normal preoperative eosinophil count of 1.1%), the patient was diagnosed in July 2020 with biopsy-proven local retroperitoneal, hepatic, diaphragmatic, and right pleural recurrence accompanied by emerging peripheral eosinophilia (WBC 17,560/uL, AEC 2,250/uL). Three weeks after starting palliative dexamethasone, pantoprazole, and buprenorphine, she was admitted on August 24, 2020 with worsening dyspnea, chest and right upper quadrant pain, mild confusion, and rapidly escalating leukocytosis and hypereosinophilia.
subjective.past_medical_history: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (pT3a, pNx, R0, M0) status post right radical nephrectomy 5 months prior (March 2020) with local/hepatic/pleural relapse in July 2020; right breast cancer treated with skin-sparing mastectomy in 2005 (no recurrence on August 2020 breast imaging); hypertension controlled on bisoprolol; no history of asthma, allergy, or alcohol abuse.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for worsening dyspnea, right chest and upper abdominal pain, and mild confusion.

objective.physical_examination: Alert with mild cognitive impairment, tachypnea, stony dullness to percussion and absent breath sounds over the right hemithorax up to the 7th intercostal space, right upper quadrant abdominal tenderness, and mild bilateral distal lower extremity edema.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission blood tests showed marked leukocytosis (WBC 40,770/uL, rising to 56,000/uL after stopping dexamethasone) with extreme hypereosinophilia (AEC 6,530/uL on admission, peaking at 18,500/uL [33% eosinophils]), mild anemia (hemoglobin 11.6 g/dL), normal platelets (346,000/uL), and elevated CRP (240 mg/L). Total serum IgE was normal (59.2 kUA/L; normal <81), MPO-ANCA was negative, and allergy and parasitic evaluations were negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Serum Aspergillus fumigatus-specific IgE was undetectable. Bone marrow biopsy excluded leukemia, and FISH testing was negative for the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene. CT pulmonary angiography demonstrated a large right pleural effusion, pneumonia, and pulmonary microembolism alongside the known retroperitoneal, hepatic, diaphragmatic, and pleural CCRCC recurrence.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Paraneoplastic leukemoid reaction and severe hypereosinophilia (AEC peaking at 18,500/uL) secondary to recurrent metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma, complicated by right malignant/parapneumonic pleural effusion and pulmonary microembolism; secondary causes of hypereosinophilia including allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (undetectable Aspergillus fumigatus-specific IgE, normal total IgE), parasitic infection, ANCA vasculitis, and FIP1L1-PDGFRA myeloid neoplasm were ruled out. Treated with thoracentesis, empirical IV antibiotics, therapeutic low-molecular-weight heparin, and a 3-day high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone pulse (1.5 g, which transiently suppressed eosinophilia); due to rapid clinical decline, she was transitioned to palliative care and died 6 months post-nephrectomy.
